key_insight: How patient event sequences are arranged during EHR pretraining can materially improve downstream prediction, even without changing the model or adding more data.
clinical_relevance: Better-pretrained EHR foundation models may deliver more accurate clinical risk predictions across multiple tasks and datasets, supporting stronger decision support tools.
method: Compared a standard global-stream pretraining setup with alternative ways of composing patient trajectories into training sequences.
Controlled how often and in what context patient histories appeared during autoregressive next-event prediction.
Evaluated the effect on downstream performance after pretraining, keeping the model and training recipe fixed.
evidence_signal: Across four MIMIC-IV v2.2 tasks, the best sequence-composition method improved macro AUROC, AUPRC, F1, and balanced accuracy, and the gains also generalized to four additional settings including INSPIRE and eICU-CRD.
watch_item: Results depend on the chosen pretraining and evaluation setup, so gains may not transfer equally to all EHR models, datasets, or deployment contexts.
paper_title: Sequence Composition in EHR Foundation Model Pretraining
